new_statements.rule_in_words: The standard reference grammar states that neither the phonetic nature nor the position of the Celtiberian word accent can be determined from the (epigraphic, syllabary-written) corpus; the only prosodic facts recoverable are that the conjunctions -kue, -ue are enclitic and the negative ne- proclitic. (A minority reconstruction, De Bernardo Stempel 2002/2012/2013/2023, operates with an inherited antepenultimate (proparoxytone) stress for Celtiberian, treating paroxytone forms as non-Celtiberian Hispano-Celtic; this is inference from syncope/vowel-assimilation in names, not a described fact, and its explicit formulation sits in her 2023 monograph, not opened.)
new_statements.exceptions: Only clitics: enclitic kue/ue, proclitic ne- (Wodtko sections 22, 49f).
new_statements.domain_note: Extinct language attested only in inscriptions (Botorrita bronzes, tesserae, coin legends) in Palaeohispanic semi-syllabary and Latin script; no accent marks; any stress claim is reconstruction.
new_statements.identity_note: Celtiberian proper (north-eastern Hispano-Celtic, celt1247). De Bernardo Stempel's 2002 accent remarks (antepenult vs later penult) concern extra-Celtiberian peninsular Hispano-Celtic onomastics (western/northern Hispania), not the Celtiberian inscriptional language itself; her Celtiberian-specific antepenult assumption appears only implicitly (2012, 2013).
